trust_decision.summary: Whether a class reference chosen by a model's saved configuration may be imported and instantiated: decided in import_module_class, which at the pinned commit trusts any model_name_or_path that exists on disk and, for every other untrusted ref, silently falls through to a bare import_from_string of the model-supplied dotted path.

landing_point.why: It is the one place that compares trust_remote_code against the model path before importing a non-sentence_transformers class ref, and its docstring (misc.py:100-102) states that a local directory is implicitly trusted — exactly the bypass the summary names.

fix_sites.entry_point: sentence_transformers.util.import_module_class (public util exported at sentence_transformers/util/__init__.py:83), reached by SentenceTransformer/CrossEncoder/SparseEncoder construction

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The trainer reload reads back the library's own checkpoint, and WordEmbeddings' tokenizer_class is a tokenizer written by save() via fullname() rather than a modules.json module class, so both read as internal plumbing the advisory's custom-module rule does not cover.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Reloading the trainer's own checkpoint for a programmatically built model whose modules.json (or nested router_config.json) names a non-sentence_transformers module class: a gate that simply raises makes load_best_model_at_end quietly keep final weights and resume_from_checkpoint crash, so the loader needs a way to accept classes already imported in-process.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: WordEmbeddings.load imports the dotted path in the module's own config.json field tokenizer_class with import_from_string and calls its load(), with no trust_remote_code check before or after the fix
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: tokenizer_class is written by this module's save() as fullname(self.tokenizer) and is not a modules.json module class, so the advisory's custom-module-class property looks like it does not reach it
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: separate package (sentence_transformers.sentence_transformer.modules vs sentence_transformers.util), two directories from the landing point, and no test in the repo exercises an untrusted tokenizer_class

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second config-driven class ref in another built-in module (e.g. a tokenizer/embedding class in StaticEmbedding, or a pooling class in Pooling)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the project already serialises class names with fullname() into module configs (word_embeddings.py:103, dense.py:85) and resolves them with import_from_string, so a new config-selectable class would copy that pattern

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second saved config file carrying its own types map next to the legacy config.json fallback at router.py:643-647
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Router already supports a legacy config filename and writes its own types map, so a v2 router config with a second resolver is plausible
